study_type_evidence.quote: Pharmacokinetic properties of 3H-radioactively labelled RD2 in male C57BL/6 mice were studied using different administration routes.
5 μl radioactively labelled peptide (5 μCi) were then added to 1 μl mouse plasma or organ homogenate supernatant.
Plasma protein binding was estimated by incubation of RD2 with varying concentrations of protein using TRANSILXL binding kits

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: male C57BL/6; age not reported; ~25 g body weight stated for the stability-assay donors
in_vivo_species.quote: Pharmacokinetic properties of 3H-radioactively labelled RD2 in male C57BL/6 mice were studied using different administration routes.

ex_vivo_detail: Mouse plasma, brain, kidney and liver homogenate supernatants were harvested from C57BL/6 mice and then incubated with 3H-RD2 (and a 3H-L-peptide control) at 37°C; proteolytic stability read out by TLC/autoradiography. Classified ex vivo per protocol because the matrices were taken out of the body before treatment.
in_vitro_detail: Cell-free plasma-protein-binding assay: constant RD2 (5 μM final) titrated against human serum albumin and α1-acid glycoprotein using TRANSILXL binding kits; KD obtained by Michaelis-Menten fit.

bioanalytical_method: Liquid scintillation counting of 3H radioactivity (disintegrations per minute) in plasma and organ homogenates; thin layer chromatography with phosphor-imaging autoradiography used separately for proteolytic-stability readout
bioanalytical_quote: 3H-radioactivity was then measured in triplicate with a liquid scintillation analyser beta radiation counter
notes: Abstract was fenced and was not used. Substance is a single peptide (RD2) given by four routes; split into one agent object per route because dose, route, tmax, Cmax/D, AUC and half-life all differ by route. PLASMA (Table II, columns read left-to-right as i.v., i.p., s.c., p.o., confirmed by the Dose row 3.3/10/10/10): tmax 3/30/30/60 min; Cmax/D 3.04/0.79/0.98/0.09 (ug/ml)/(mg/kg); AUC0-28 1.95/4.54/5.39/4.51 mg/ml*min; t1/2 59/62/60/58 h; lambda-z 0.00020/0.00019/0.00019/0.00020 min-1; bioavailability F 76.9 (i.p.), 91.4 (s.c.), 76.5 (p.o.) %. BRAIN (Table III, same column order): tmax 3/30/20/60 min; Cmax/D 0.06 for every route; AUC0-28 1.48/3.37/4.51/4.49 mg/g*min; t1/2 60/61/94/73 h. Brain half-lives are recorded here rather than in the agent objects because half_life_matrix is set to plasma. Note a small internal inconsistency: the Results prose states brain t1/2 of "61 h (i.v. and i.p.)" whereas Table III lists 60 h for i.v. and 61 h for i.p.; the table values are reported above. Also note the body prose gives brain Cmax/D units as (ug/ml)/(mg/kg) while Table III heads the same row (ug/g)/(mg/kg); the table unit is the physically consistent one. NO ABSORPTION HALF-LIFE and no rate constant ka is reported anywhere in the body - only the terminal elimination rate constant lambda-z, from which the authors themselves computed t1/2 = ln2/lambda-z; that published terminal half-life is what is recorded, no conversion was performed by the extractor. Cmax is reported only dose-normalised (Cmax/D); absolute Cmax is never printed, so the normalised value with its units is recorded verbatim. Analysis was non-compartmental, so no separate absorption/distribution phase half-lives exist. Additional untreated animals (n = 3) received no RD2 and served only as blank references, so they are not listed as an agent. Human serum albumin and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein are in vitro binding reagents, not administered agents, and are likewise not listed.
